title: Skeletal dashboard pruning + graceful fallbacks for trace & cost tiles
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: PRD excerpt + decisions log for reducing the initial Console telemetry surface to a skeletal set of dashboard tiles and tiered tracing/cost fallbacks. The goal is to ship a coherent, usable Console alpha that meets latency and cost telemetry needs while deferring lower-value drilldowns and heavy-card visualizations. This ticket captures scope removals, exact acceptance criteria for the trimmed MVP, and the operational fallback rules that keep the Console reliable under quota/telemetry sampling constraints.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard launch surface limited to 6 tiles: service health, request rate, median latency, 95th latency (route-level toggle), daily cost snapshot, and top-3 cost contributors (route/model). No additional drilldown panels required in alpha.
Tracing overview uses 10% sampling by default with an opt-in 50% mode behind a dev flag; trace collection does not increase customer observed latency > 2ms per request on average.
Cost breakdown tile presents an aggregated daily cost and a delta vs. baseline; detailed per-token waterfall is deferred to console-2026.2.

If telemetry retention budget is exceeded or ingestion backlog > 2 minutes, Console falls back to summary-only tiles and disables trace flamegraphs; users see a clear degradations banner with a link to 'why data is missing'.
Telemetry query time-to-first-byte (TTFB) for dashboard loads must be < 700ms 90th percentile in staging with 50 simulated orgs and realistic traffic profiles.
Rollout gated by canary: 10% of orgs for first 48 hours, automated rollback if dashboard error rate > 1% or query latency regression > 20% vs baseline.
Docs and minimal in-console help text added explaining sampling, aggregation windows, and how cost numbers are computed (linkable).
Design QA: tiles align to mobile breakpoint baseline (no overlapping elements) and accept 'skeleton' placeholder states for delayed cards.
Operations: alert runbook created for 'telemetry ingestion backlog' and assigned to oncall team with playbook steps and contact links.

decisions: Ship a single consolidated cost tile rather than separate model/route cost tiles for MVP to reduce ingestion/query cardinality.
Defer per-route 95th latency drilldown to a later milestone; offer a route-level toggle that shows a small sample list only.
Implement sample-rate opt-in behind feature flag rather than full open control in alpha to reduce support surface.
risks: Users accustomed to deep cost attribution will find MVP insufficient — mitigated by explicit roadmap and in-console link to full billing exports.
Sampling may hide rare but critical latency regressions; addressed by preserving sampling-based alerting on high-quantile regressions and targeted full-sample traces for canaries.
Aggregation pipeline delay could show stale cost deltas; acceptance includes clear UX messaging when numbers are estimated or delayed.
